title: Prime Number Verification
description:
Write a function named `is_prime(n)` that accepts a positive integer `n` and returns `True` if `n` is a prime number, and `False` otherwise.

A prime number is a natural number greater than 1 whose only divisors are 1 and itself.
constraints: The function must return a boolean value (True / False)
Time complexity is expected to be optimal (O(sqrt(N)))

title: Two Sum: Target Pair Index
description:
Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`.

You may assume that each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice. Return the indices as a list `[index1, index2]`.

title: Valid Parentheses Sequence
description:
Given a string `s` containing just the characters `(`, `)`, `{`, `}`, `[` and `]`, determine if the input string is valid.

An input string is valid if open brackets are closed by the same type of brackets and closed in the correct order.

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
description:
Given a string `s`, return the longest palindromic substring in `s`.

A string is palindromic if it reads the same forward and backward.
constraints: s consist of only digits and English letters.
starterCode:
def longest_palindrome(s):
    # Implement longest palindrome search
    if not s:
        return ""
        
    start, max_len = 0, 1
    for i in range(len(s)):
        # Odd-length check
        l, r = i, i
        while l >= 0 and r < len(s) and s[l] == s[r]:
            if r - l + 1 > max_len:
                start = l
                max_len = r - l + 1
            l -= 1
            r += 1
            
    return s[start:start + max_len]

# Sample execution
print(longest_palindrome("babad"))
